Charles, Charles Abila, Ramon Abila, J. Sheeham. Kodak colour-calibration bar along the bottom edge (Huntington digitization).

primary_source_newspaper_TARGET1.title_verbatim: HOPE TO SAVE CATTLE FROM THE TEXAS TICK
primary_source_newspaper_TARGET1.publication: Los Angeles Herald, Volume 35, Number 238, 27 May 1908, page 10 (dateline SANTA ANA, May 26)
primary_source_newspaper_TARGET1.repository: California Digital Newspaper Collection (CDNC), UC Riverside
primary_source_newspaper_TARGET1.ocr_text_verbatim: SANTA ANA, May 26.—Dr. Coleman of Los Angeles, deputy state quarantine officer, was here today in consultation with Orange county cattle raisers on the subject of protection of their herds from the Texas tick. Within the last ten days several hundred head of stock have been treated by dipping at the ranch of J. C. Joplin in Trabuco canyon, six or seven hundred head are now being dipped at Capistrano and dipping is in progress at Yorba and at the Bixby ranch in Santa Ana canyon. Dr. Coleman speaks hopefully of the prospect of eradicating the cattle pest and predicts that Orange county herds will soon be given a clean bill of health.
primary_source_newspaper_TARGET1.significance: This is the primary source underlying the previously-reported 'four 1908 Orange County dipping sites' (Joplin/Trabuco Canyon, Capistrano, Yorba, Bixby/Santa Ana Canyon). It names the state official (Dr. Coleman, deputy state quarantine officer). NONE of the four dipping sites is attributed to the O'Neill / Mission Viejo / Santa Margarita ranch. Grade B2 (reputable newspaper quoting a named official).
primary_source_newspaper_TARGET1.geographic_note: J. C. Joplin's cattle were dipped 'in Trabuco canyon' — Trabuco Canyon lies within/adjacent to the O'Neill Rancho Trabuco, but the herd and dipping are attributed to Joplin (a lessee/rancher), not to the O'Neill operation.

false_friend_flag.item: Map of the Mission Viejo or La Purisima Rancho [Calif.] ... Ralph W. Norris, May 1859 (UC Berkeley, Bancroft Library, Land Case Map D-1024, ark:/13030/hb9n39p2gd)
false_friend_flag.warning: This is NOT the Orange County O'Neill Rancho Mission Viejo. It is 'Rancho La Misión Vieja de la Purísima', confirmed to Joaquín & José Carrillo, at approx. W 120°28'/N 34°37' — i.e. SANTA BARBARA COUNTY (Lompoc / La Purísima Mission area). The O'Neill OC ranch's own Mexican grant was 'Rancho Misión Vieja o La Paz' (Forster), a different land-case map. Do not conflate.
